sources.content: Lunderpike .cursorrules. Lunderpike measures search relevance by replaying judged queries against a search engine and computing NDCG and recall. The code is Python 3.11, with a small FastAPI service in `service/` and the scoring library in `lunderpike/`. Use `make setup` to create the virtual environment and `make test` to run tests. Judgment lists live in `judgments/` as CSV files with the columns `query`, `doc_id` and `grade`. Grades run from 0 (irrelevant) to 3 (perfect). The default cutoff for metrics is 10 results.

Rules. Do not change a judgment file once a report has used it; add a new file with a date suffix such as `shoes-2026-11.csv`. Reports go to `reports/` as HTML and must not be committed. The service runs on port 8420 and has no authentication, so it must bind only to localhost. Keep scoring functions free of I/O. When you add a metric, add it to `METRICS` in `lunderpike/registry.py` and write a test with a hand-computed expected value.

claims.text: Lunderpike relevance grades run from 0 to 3.
The Lunderpike service runs on port 8420.
Lunderpike reports should be committed to the repository.
The default Lunderpike metric cutoff is 20 results.
Lunderpike judgment lists are CSV files.
New Lunderpike metrics are added to METRICS in lunderpike/registry.py.
